chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a man performing the Maghrib prayer when evening comes upon him at 'Arafah.

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man; the legally responsible person mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.بِعَرَفَةَ: at 'Arafah, the well-known place of hajj
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform the Maghrib prayer at 'Arafah when evening arrives?
ai.summary: This hadith states that there is no objection to a person praying Maghrib when evening arrives while he is at 'Arafah. It addresses a jurisprudential ruling connected to the rites and timing of prayer during hajj.
